Fusillade

FYOO-suh-lahd · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Fusillade is a rapid series of shots fired, especially all at once or in quick succession.

A fusillade of bottle rockets erupted over the lake at exactly midnight.

Worked Example

The general ordered a fusillade to cover the retreating troops as they crossed the bridge.

This wasn't a single shot -- it was a rapid burst of many shots fired together, which is exactly a fusillade.

How Fusillade Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

barrage

barrage: a concentrated, rapid outpouring, often of gunfire

volley

volley: a number of shots or missiles fired at the same time

Antonyms

ceasefire

ceasefire: a temporary stop to fighting

How Strong Is It? — shot → bombardment → fusillade

shot vs. fusillade

shot vs. fusillade: A single shot is one report; a fusillade is many shots fired rapidly, one after another or all at once.

bombardment vs. fusillade

bombardment vs. fusillade: A fusillade is a rapid burst of small-arms fire; a bombardment is a sustained, heavier assault, often with artillery.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Fusillade comes from French fusiller ('to shoot'), itself from fusil ('a flintlock gun'), plus -ade, a suffix marking an action or its result.

Use the root in a new word: fusillade

Use the root in a new word: fusillade: French fusil traces back to a Vulgar Latin word for fire-striking steel -- a fittingly explosive origin, though it left no common surviving English word family beyond fusillade itself.

Root Check

Word Choice

Fusillade can describe literal gunfire or, in a non-literal sense, any rapid, overwhelming burst -- a fusillade of questions, a fusillade of complaints.
